original.target_description: Context-based Collocation Task; mixed-model ANOVA comparing native controls, L3 Spanish, and L3 Portuguese, with preposed/postposed item type. Specific target test unresolved.

n.sample_role: Candidate common-model N = 60 participants; retained in dispositions only pending row/test identification. Item/token counts are not participant N.
n.exclusions: L3 participants selected for advanced to near-native L2 proficiency and intermediate L3 proficiency (pp.116–117). All participants completed the experimental tasks (p.117). No further task-specific exclusions reported in the inspected participant and results sections.
n.location: PDF pp.10–12, printed pp.116–118, V.1 Participants and methodology and VI Results
n.quote:
A total of 60 subjects participated in this study. The control group consisted of 33 native
speakers of Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese (n = 17 Spanish and n = 16 Brazilian Por-
tuguese) and there were two L3 subject groups both at the intermediate level for the L3:
Italian natives of L2 English learning Spanish as an L3 (n = 12) and English-native L2
Spanish learners of L3 Portuguese (n = 15). ... Each of the analyses compares
the performance of the three participant groups – the native control and the two L3
groups – using a mixed-model ANOVA.

notes: The supplied original locator p.13 identifies Context-based Collocation Task, but the neutral description does not distinguish the interaction, item-type main effect, or language-group main effect. Multiple candidate tests are printed. No row order, numerical matching, or replication locator was used to choose among them. Printed candidates (all F statistics; all paired p values are exact equalities): item type × group: F(2,57) = .288, p = .751; item type: F(1,57) = 2.526, p = .118; language group: F(2,57) = 0.272, p = 0.763. Candidate analytic participant N: 17 Spanish native controls + 16 Brazilian Portuguese native controls + 12 L3 Spanish learners + 15 L3 Portuguese learners = 60; equivalently 33 pooled native controls + 12 + 15 = 60. The source explicitly identifies these mutually exclusive groups and says each analysis compares the pooled native-control group and the two L3 groups. This is not inferred from degrees of freedom. Retained only as a candidate pending row/test identification. L3 participants selected for advanced to near-native L2 proficiency and intermediate L3 proficiency (pp.116–117). All participants completed the experimental tasks (p.117). No further task-specific exclusions reported in the inspected participant and results sections. Supplied PDF pages 10–13 were visually inspected; quotes use supplied canonical text. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders.
